metadata.title: Frobenius Minimality, Minimum-Layer Uniqueness, and an Infinite Family of Huneke-Wiegand Counterexamples
metadata.description:
Son Pham publicly identified a counterexample to the Huneke-Wiegand conjecture in the class of two-generated monomial ideals over symmetric numerical semigroup rings, subsequently verified by Professor Craig Huneke. We preserve that discovery priority and answer two different questions: how small can such an example be, and does the same semigroup/ideal class contain an explicit infinite family? We prove by proof-carrying exact computation that the least Frobenius number is 181, attained by Pham's semigroup at ideal shift 14. First, an implementation of the complete Blanco-Rosales tree exhausts all 48,954 symmetric semigroups with Frobenius number below 69 and all 1,503,391 associated gap cases. An independent Boolean route checks 1,156 fixed-pair UNSAT certificates for the same range. We then introduce a one-hot shift-selector CNF that asks one existence question per Frobenius number. Its DRAT certificates exclude every odd value from 69 through 179, while the formula at 181 is satisfiable and decodes exactly to the public semigroup and shift. A separately generated fixed-pair formula returns the same model. An independent verification rehashes all 228 files in the minimality search, totaling 760,081,739 bytes, rechecks both SAT models, and reproduces the strict-order manifest with no mismatch. Complete theorem-tree enumeration at F=69,71,73,75 provides an object-level cross-check on another 79,790 semigroups and 2,933,163 gap cases. A second projected enumeration proves that shift 14 is the only feasible shift at F=181 and that the public membership vector is the only semigroup there. An independent verification of the 12 files of this classification rechecks both terminal DRAT proofs. Thus Pham's pair is the unique normalized pair attaining the Frobenius minimum in this class.

Turning to the second question, for every integer p ≥ 4 we construct a symmetric numerical semigroup Γ_p of multiplicity 24p, Frobenius number 78p-1, conductor 78p, and embedding dimension 11p, for which I_p=(t^(24p),t^(30p)) is nonprincipal and rigid. This family theorem is deductive: seven exact interval-sum identities prove closure, symmetry, and D_s=E_s+E_s; a finite sweep through p=300 and an independent re-implementation are supporting checks. For every family member we also determine the value semigroup of the endomorphism ring exactly. It has multiplicity 24p, Frobenius number 54p-1, conductor 54p, genus 38p-1, and embedding dimension 12p. It is nonsymmetric, and the endomorphism ring is strictly larger than the original ring. Recent endomorphism-center criteria then show uniformly that the ideal remains rigid over its endomorphism ring but is not reflexive there, with the adjacent Ext and Tor obstruction groups nonzero. We further prove that this endomorphism semigroup has Cohen-Macaulay type and reduced type 10p, hence maximal reduced type, and that its completed semigroup ring is not almost Gorenstein. The traces of the ideal and its endomorphism ring both equal the conductor of the finite birational extension. We determine that common value ideal exactly and prove the identity ℓ_(R_p)(R_p/(R_p:E_p)) = ℓ_(R_p)(E_p/R_p) = p+1. The equality of the two lengths is a general consequence of one-dimensional Gorenstein local duality, while the exact common ideal and its value p+1 are the family-specific data. We further prove that this conductor is nonstable and compute its complete one-step stability defect: ℓ_(R_p)(T_p^2/t^(4s)T_p) = 14p. The full reduction sequence is also exact: t^(4s)R_p is a minimal reduction of T_p with reduction number four, successive Sally-quotient lengths 23p-1, 14p, 2p, 1, 0, and Hilbert-Samuel coefficients e_0(T_p)=24p and e_1(T_p)=39p.

The associated graded ring of T_p nevertheless has depth zero: its complete Valabrega-Valla module is concentrated in one degree, where it has length p. We compute the exact Hilbert series and show that its numerator has only positive coefficients despite this failure of Cohen-Macaulayness. We then determine the complete zeroth local cohomology: it is k^p, concentrated in degree zero and annihilated by the full homogeneous maximal ideal. Hence the tangent cone is Buchsbaum but not Cohen-Macaulay, with unbounded Buchsbaum invariant p; its quotient by the finite-length torsion is Cohen-Macaulay with an exact Hilbert series. Over the polynomial Noether normalization induced by the minimal reduction, we determine the entire graded module: the torsion consists of p exponent-one cyclic summands, while the free quotient has rank 24p and explicit shifts. This yields the complete minimal resolution, projective dimension one, regularity four, top-local-cohomology a-invariant three, and the exact parameter-section identity ℓ(G_p/x_pG_p) = 25p = e_0(T_p)+I(G_p). The exact identity T_p^2=m_pT_p identifies the special fiber canonically with G_p/H^0(G_p). It is Cohen-Macaulay of type 10p+1, but its Artinian socle lies in degrees two and four, so it is neither level nor Gorenstein. We then determine its defining ideal: in the polynomial ring on its 10p minimal degree-one generators, it has exactly 50p^2-17p minimal quadrics and the single additional cubic X_0^2X_(3p)-X_p^3, with no other minimal equation. Thus its relation type is three and it is not Koszul. The all-parameter component calculation is an exact Presburger verification, supported by a separately encoded graph check; it relies on the soundness of the solver, whose UNSAT answers carry no independently checked proof.

From the same exact h-vector, Artinian socle, and first Betti row, we then determine the homological edges over the full presentation ring. Its projective dimension is 10p-1, its regularity is four, β_(2,3) = 2p(500p^2-330p+31)/3, the complete last row has ranks 10p in shift c+2 and one in shift c+4 for c=10p-1, and β_(c-1,c+3)=8p. The canonical module has 10p minimal generators in degree -1 and one in degree -3. We then determine the first previously unknown interior strand. With the offset grading deg X_a=(1,a), β_(2,4)=8p and β_(3,4) = p(5p-1)(500p^2-440p+47)/2, and the 8p second syzygies occur with multiplicity one exactly at offsets {3p+a : a ∈ ℰ_(p,1), a ≥ 6p}. Relative squarefree-divisor chains and an integral unit matching give the upper bound; an exact quadratic colon and minimal mapping cone give the matching lower bound. We then complete the second Betti row. The only remaining possible entries are β_(2,5)=p(2p-3) and β_(2,6)=0. The degree-five support is the union of three explicit intervals, with pair-sum multiplicities on the outer blocks and a plateau profile on the middle block. An integral offset matching gives a unit Smith form, so the result again holds over every field. This completes one homological row, not the remaining Betti table.

We next determine the degree-five third syzygies. If H_p={a ∈ ℰ_(p,1) : a ≥ 6p}, then β_(3,(5,b)) = #{{a,c} ⊂ H_p : a<c, a+c=b-3p} and β_(3,5)=4p(8p-1). The support is [15p+1,39p-3] ∖ {33p-1}. An integral normal form leaves a primitive free basis indexed by unordered pairs of the 8p high cubic-colon variables. Combining this with the complete second row and the Hilbert numerator gives β_(4,5) = 2p(5p-1)(10p-3)(100p^2-110p+13)/3, completing internal degree five over every field. We also identify the complete cubic-colon quotient with the canonical idealization of the p-th Veronese rational normal curve ring. Its multigraded Hilbert numerator and an integral relative normal form give β_(3,6) = 8p(7p^2-12p+2)/3 over every field, with support [3p+4,29p-5] ∖ ([6p-3,6p+1] ∪ [9p-3,9p]). In total degree seven, a zero-vertex Boolean matching leaves only triangles at the single residual hole 6p-1. Adjoining a missing vertex from {1,2,3,4} gives each one a same-offset tetrahedron whose reduced boundary has that triangle as its unique critical face with coefficient ±1. Hence β_(3,7)=0 integrally, and the complete third row over every field is β_(3,4) = p(5p-1)(500p^2-440p+47)/2, β_(3,5) = 4p(8p-1), β_(3,6) = 8p(7p^2-12p+2)/3, β_(3,7) = 0, with no other shifts. Its total rank is β_3 = p(7500p^3-7988p^2+2025p-133)/6.

The same canonical idealization determines much more about the cubic-colon quotient D_p=P_p/(q_p:f_p). Put c=2p-2, m=8p, and λ_(c,a) = c·binom(c,a) - binom(c,a+1) - binom(c,a-1). Its complete graded Betti polynomial is B_(D_p)^(P_p)(x,z) = (1+xz)^m (1 + Σ_(a=1)^(c-1) λ_(c,a) x^a z^(a+1) + x^c z^(c+2)). Hence every free-module rank and shift is known over every field, with projective dimension 10p-2 and regularity two. A colon-intersection pullback then proves that the quadratic quotient A_p=P_p/q_p has depth one and regularity two. The grading gap makes the cubic mapping cone minimal, so B_(C_p)^(P_p)(x,z) = B_(A_p)^(P_p)(x,z) + xz^3 B_(D_p)^(P_p)(x,z). Consequently the complete regularity-three and regularity-four strands of the special fiber are explicit binomial convolutions of the displayed colon polynomial, over every field. This removes every comparison-rank ambiguity from the cubic cone.

For the lower strands, put τ_p = 8p-1+p(p+1)/2. The Artinian reduction of the high-variable kernel is a two-layer incidence module. Its first missing offset gives a unique primitive cokernel cell, and a separate unit pivot proves that the connecting map from the colon quotient cannot hit it. Thus, over every field, β_(p,(p+2,τ_p))(K_p) = β_(p,(p+2,τ_p))(A_p) = β_(p,(p+2,τ_p))(C_p) = 1. We then classify every primitive zero row of the incidence cokernel. If R_b={g : b-g ∈ H_p}, the coordinate e_F ⊗ v_b is a zero row exactly when R_b ⊆ F, giving a closed free-summand count in every homological degree. The block b=10p+t, 2 ≤ t ≤ p-2, supplies consecutive kernel classes in degrees p+1,...,2p-3. The first connecting cell does not repeat the unit-pivot mechanism, but its complete target quotient exposes characteristic dependence: β_(5,(7,87))(A_4) = β_(5,(7,87))(C_4) = 4 over F_2 and 3 over F_3. The corresponding integral kernel cokernel is ℤ^4 ⊕ ℤ/2ℤ. This determines exact lower-strand points and a characteristic-dependent multigraded cell. Exact complete-target calculations extend the phenomenon through (p,t)=(9,2). On the tested t=2 diagonal with 5 ≤ p ≤ 9, the kernel cokernel has the same dimension over F_2 and F_3, while the connecting image is smaller over F_2; the resulting excesses are 4, 9, 18, 31, 49. Two formulas suggested by shorter initial segments are refuted by the later values. For every p ≥ 4 and 2 ≤ t ≤ p-2, a separate offset inequality shows that the shifted cubic source is absent, so the exact quadratic-quotient and special-fiber values agree at every target in this family. This is not an infinite characteristic-dependence theorem. The results do not determine the two complete lower strands, the differential matrices, or the full special-fiber resolution. The results remain confined to two-generated monomial ideals over symmetric numerical semigroup rings and do not classify arbitrary Gorenstein domains and modules.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/commutative-algebra/huneke-wiegand).
metadata.description_addendum: Version 0.15 completes the second graded Betti row of the conductor special fiber for every p>=4 and over every field: beta_(2,5)=p(2p-3), beta_(2,6)=0, with the complete three-block multigraded support and multiplicity profile. Integral lexicographic matching and unit Smith normal forms prove characteristic independence. Higher interior rows remain open.
metadata.version_notes: Editorial revision. The text states the mathematics and the supporting computations without process commentary: the working vocabulary of the programme is replaced by the scientific terms (computation, independent recomputation, negative controls, a stated time limit); anecdotes about superseded implementations are removed; the p=24 case of the bounded state-graph computation for the defining ideal is stated as a passing run without independent recomputation, outside the verified range p=4,...,23; the claim labels [MV+D] and [D/MV] are defined in the introduction next to [MV] and [D]; the field in the abstract is set in the same blackboard-bold symbol as in the body; the two refuted tail formulas for v(T_p) and v(T_p^2) are stated as remarks; computations are cited by their record identifiers, and the data-availability section states what the identifiers and the printed SHA-256 aggregates denote. The abstract and the scope section no longer chain clauses added version by version. The toolchain table becomes a captioned float with ragged-right cells, a forced page break that left half a page empty is removed, centred displays stay with the sentence that introduces them, the record title now matches the capitalization of the printed title, and a page-1 header block states the document type, version, licence and DOIs (the attribution of the counterexample to Son Pham remains in the abstract, the introduction, the scope section and the acknowledgments). Theorem statements, formulas, table values, hashes and references are unchanged, and proofs change only in the wording around the computations they cite. Methods, data, results and conclusions are unchanged.
